To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the GPAC is a very unstable statistic, (2) the GPAC has a very high false detection rate for AR models of moderate order, and (3) the GPAC cannot be recommended as a reliable means to detect MA components.

the GPAC has unstable behavior when used on real data of moderate length, that it is not suitable for the order identification of MA processes, and that it can only be recommended for confirming an AR fit to a data series.
the GPAC is not a useful tool for order identification of ARMA models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of order determination for ARMA processes.
the use of the General Partial autocorrelation Function as a tool for the identification of the order of the autoregressive and moving average parts of a time series.
the use of a general partial autocorrelation function for the order determination in ARMA(p,q) models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of the GPAC for order determination is not recommended.
the GPAC should not be used as a means to identify the orders p and q of an ARMA(p, q) model.
the GPAC is a very useful tool in the context of AR models and that it is a very unreliable tool in the context and application of ARMA(p, 0) or ARMA(0, q) models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GPAC should not be used as an order identification tool in ARMA models.
the GPAC is a good diagnostic tool for AR processes but a poor diagnostic tool for MA processes.
the GPAC is an unstable and unreliable tool for order identification in real series.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the GPAC should be avoided in practice, and that other tools, such as the Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroscedasticity (GARCH) and the Partial Autocorrelations of the Residuals of the Autoregressive Model (PARA), should be used instead.
the use of the GPAC in order identification of ARMA models is not recommended.
the GPAC should be used with caution and that the use of the sample ACF and PACF is still the preferred approach for model identification.
